headline: Paraguay's Two-Minute Coup Withstands Türkiye's Onslaught
story: Türkiye controlled this match from the third minute onward. Paraguay scored in the second—a flash of clinical ruthlessness that stunned the San Francisco crowd—and then retreated into a defensive shell. The home side pressed forward relentlessly, accumulating 32 shots and 68% possession, but Paraguay's shape held firm. The arrival of a red card for Paraguay at 45+3 should have turned this decisively in Türkiye's favor, yet even with ten men, they would not break through.

Expected goals exposed the gulf: Türkiye's 2.13 against Paraguay's 0.36. Yet Paraguay's goalkeeper and defensive unit earned every plaudit, denying Türkiye multiple clear-cut chances across ninety minutes, including one worth 0.44 xG late in the game. Julio Enciso's 7.9 rating embodied Paraguay's attacking threat, while their defensive discipline—reflected in an 18.4-second ball recovery time—strangled Türkiye's rhythm. Türkiye's own 7.1-second recovery pace could not compensate for a lack of clinical finishing in a match that will haunt their campaign.

keyMoment.text: Paraguay's second-minute goal from 0.03 xG set tone for Türkiye's labored afternoon of plenty and little to show.

home.verdict: Dominance without efficiency was their undoing.
points: Missed 0.44 xG chance in 89th minute—the one that would have forced Paraguay into genuine distress.
32 shots and 2.13 xG revealed poor conversion efficiency—the real deficit was in the final third.
Conceding in second minute forfeited control of match narrative and tempo from the start.

away.verdict: A smash-and-grab that survived both good fortune and a numerical disadvantage.
points: Julio Enciso's 7.9 rating delivered: one clinical intervention in a match of few chances.
Played final 45 minutes with ten men yet conceded nothing—defensive discipline won the day.
0.03 xG goal was fortunate, but fortune rewarded bravery and a composed defensive shape.

statLine: Türkiye's 32 shots and 2.13 expected goals could not overcome Paraguay's one lethal intervention and ten-man discipline.
